description: Changes the connector's account's My Gear, in one call. add puts new pieces in; one the account already holds (same brand, name and variant) comes back as already_have and is left as it was. update changes pieces by the ids get_my_gear gives, only the fields sent, null clearing one. A piece that names a catalog_id, as it is added or later, is linked to that catalog row and takes its brand, name, variant, gear type and weight where none were given; null unlinks it. remove puts pieces away by id: they stop being offered on lists, and the lists that still carry them will not bring them back. restore brings put-away pieces back. kit, on a piece added or updated, makes it a kit of other pieces by id (replacing what it held), and null on update turns a kit back into a single piece; a kit's weight is its items', so a kit takes own_weight_g, never weight_g. Each piece answers for itself, in the order sent, with a reason when it wasn't done as sent. What is added or changed here counts as the owner's own word on the piece, so a list saved later cannot overwrite it. Needs read-and-change access.

add.description: New pieces, each with a name or a catalog_id.

catalog_id.description: A catalog row from search_catalog. The piece takes the catalog's brand, name, variant, gear type and weight, each unless given here; a name can be left out.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for price, such as USD. Ignored without a price.

gear_type.description: What kind of thing it is: Tent, Quilt.

kit.description: Makes the piece a KIT: a set kept together, such as a cook kit or a sleep system, that weighs its own weight plus its items'. items REPLACES whatever it held: pieces of My Gear by id, each with how many, none of them a kit (kits are one level deep), and a piece already in a kit can't become one. A piece can be in several kits. Not with weight_g: set own_weight_g for what the kit weighs by itself.

count.description: How many of it the kit holds. Default 1, and never more than the piece's owned: a higher count is held to it, so raise owned first.

id.description: A piece of My Gear, from get_my_gear.

own_weight_g.description: What the kit weighs by itself, a stuff sack or a strap, in grams. Default 0.

name.description: The product or item name, without brand or variant.

owned.description: How many of it the owner has, when more than one: three of the same bottle is one piece with owned 3, not three pieces.

price.description: What one cost, in the currency's main unit: 199.95.

product_url.description: The maker's or a shop's page for it.

weight_g.description: Grams for one. 0 records it as not weighed yet.

A piece can be in several kits. Not with weight_g: set own_weight_g for what the kit weighs by itself. Null turns a kit back into a single piece, weighing what the kit did; its items stay as the pieces they are.

name: edit_my_gear

added.description: Pieces that were new to My Gear.

removed.description: One per id in remove, then one per id in restore, in the order sent.

results.description: One per piece in add, in the order sent.

catalog_id.description: The catalog row the piece is linked to; null when it isn't.

classification.description: base, worn or consumable; null when the owner leaves it to each list.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of price, when one was recorded.

display_name.description: Brand, name and variant joined, the way the gear page shows a piece. User text.

in_kits.description: The ids of the kits this piece is in; empty when none.

kind.description: The section the gear page files it under, read from its icon or gear type: Shelter, Sleep, Kitchen, Clothing and the like; Food, which the gear page keeps on a Food tab of its own, read by calories; Other when nothing matches; and Kits for a kit. Not set by hand.

kit.description: Null on a single piece. On a KIT, a set the owner keeps together: what it weighs by itself (a stuff sack) and the items it holds, each also a piece of My Gear by its own id. Its weight_g already counts them, so put a kit on a list either as one row or as its items, never both.

count.description: How many of it the kit holds.

id.description: The item's own id in My Gear.

put_away.description: Removed from My Gear: still listed in the kit, no longer counted in its weight.

own_weight_g.description: What the kit weighs by itself, in grams; usually 0.

last_used.description: When a list last carried it, ISO 8601.

owned.description: How many of this piece the owner has: three of the same bottle is one piece with owned 3. Not how many a trip carries, which is a list row's qty, nor how many a kit holds, which is its item's count. The gear page's totals count one of each.

price.description: What one cost, in the currency's main unit.

times_used.description: How many list saves have carried this piece into My Gear.

weight_g.description: Grams for one, to a tenth; 0 when it has never been weighed. On a kit, the whole kit: its items plus its own weight.

reason.description: Why an entry was not done as sent, in a sentence.

status.description: already_have: the same brand, name and variant is there already, untouched, and item is that piece. invalid: no name, or a kit that could not be made. full: My Gear is at its ceiling.
